translations.answer: Map velocity error to reward. If the target area curve is too flat, switch to a linear term or narrower exponential kernel. Check energy, posture, and torque penalties to ensure they do not overshadow velocity reward. After modification, evaluate velocity, energy, and fall rate to avoid sacrificing impact for speed.
translations.applicability: Applicable to locomotion policies trained with expected velocity.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Raise height reward first, then increase posture and smoothness constraints.
translations.details.attempts.1: Switch velocity tracking to a steeper or linear error reward.
translations.details.attempts.2: Increase landing posture and impact penalty during jumps.
translations.details.attempts.3: Add intermediate rewards for height changes and gradually increase difficulty.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Break rewards into main objective, auxiliary objective, and penalty terms, and observe height, posture, joint velocity, foot contact, and landing phase.
translations.details.environments.0: Gym humanoid reinforcement learning environment; basic actions for standing, walking, and jumping; specific robot and code versions not provided.
translations.details.limits.0: Example weights and thresholds cannot be directly transferred to different robots; code snippet is pseudocode, needs verification of units, symbols, and contact definitions.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Main text provides symptom—causality—tuning direction table, but no public independent replication or quantitative comparison before and after.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Standing strategy uses high-frequency jitter to boost reward without actually standing.
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Walking strategy does not reach target speed.
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Jumping strategy fails to stabilize after landing.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before testing on real robot, check torque, action rate, contact impact, and joint limits in simulation. Use cradle, limit force, and emergency stop after inspection.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Joint velocity penalty is too heavy.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Velocity reward curve is too flat.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Robot oscillates or remains at local optimum.
translations.media_summaries.0: Key evidence is primarily formulas, pseudocode, and symptom-to-tuning tables; no verified training curves provided in images, so images are not considered as evidence.
translations.source.locator: Section 3 on velocity tracking and Section 6 on tuning table
translations.source.title: Local Optima and Stage-wise Tuning in Humanoid Base Action Reward Functions
translations.title: Walking Strategy Continuously Fails to Reach Target Speed: Which Reward Design Should Be Checked?
